The '''2018–19 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team''' represented [[Purdue University]] in the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Their head coach was [[Matt Painter]] in his 14th season with the Boilers. The team played their home games at [[Mackey Arena]] in [[West Lafayette, Indiana]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. With a win over Northwestern on March 9, 2019, the Boilermakers clinched a share of the [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten regular season]] championship, the school's 24th championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2019/03/09/purdue-basketball-beats-northwestern-lock-up-share-big-ten-title/3105838002/|title=Purdue basketball beats Northwestern to lock up share of Big Ten championship|website=Journal & Courier|language=en|access-date=2019-03-19}}</ref> They finished the season 26–10, 16–4 in [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to win a share of the Big Ten regular season championship, the school's conference-record 24th championship. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2019 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they were upset by [[2018–19 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]] in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game?gameId=401120735|title=Minnesota vs. Purdue - Game Summary - March 15, 2019 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-03-31}}</ref> The received an at-large bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 3 seed in the South region. They defeated [[2018–19 Old Dominion Monarchs basketball team|Old Dominion]], 61–48, in the first round<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123399|title=Old Dominion vs. Purdue – Game Recap – March 21, 2019 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-03-31}}</ref> before beating defending champion [[2018–19 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]], 87–61, to advance to the Sweet Sixteen.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123432|title=Villanova vs. Purdue – Game Recap – March 23, 2019 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-03-31}}</ref> In the Sweet Sixteen, they defeated [[2018–19 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]], 99–94 in overtime, to advance to the Elite Eight.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2019/03/28/tennessee-vols-basketball-purdue-ncaa-tournament-rick-barnes/3263933002/|title=Tennessee basketball races back against Purdue, then falls in overtime in Sweet 16|website=Knoxville News Sentinel|language=en|access-date=2019-03-31|archive-date=2019-03-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190329140832/https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2019/03/28/tennessee-vols-basketball-purdue-ncaa-tournament-rick-barnes/3263933002/|url-status=dead}}</ref> There they lost to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|eventual champion]] [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]], 80–75 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/31/sports/ncaa-tournament-virginia-purdue.html|title=Virginia Fends Off Purdue and Naysayers to Reach the Final Four|last=Depaolo|first=Joe|date=2019-03-31|work=The New York Times|access-date=2019-03-31|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

On October 12, 2018, Purdue signed Matt Painter to a rolling two-year contract extension, through the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/24965919/purdue-boilermakers-extend-coach-matt-painter-2023-24-season|title=Purdue extends Painter through 2023-24 season|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-11-08|language=en}}</ref> Following the conclusion of the regular season, Painter was named the Big Ten Coach of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2019/03/11/purdue-basketballs-matt-painter-voted-big-ten-coach-year/3127376002/|title=Purdue basketball's Matt Painter wins Big Ten Coach of the Year for fourth time|website=Journal & Courier|language=en|access-date=2019-03-31}}</ref>

== Offseason ==

=== Departures ===
On March 26, 2018, sophomore guard [[Carsen Edwards]] announced he would enter the [[2018 NBA draft|NBA draft]], but would not sign with an agent.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.landof10.com/purdue/carsen-edwards-nba-draft-agent-purdue-basketball-stats-bio|title=Purdue's Carsen Edwards enters 2018 NBA Draft process, does not hire agent|date=2018-03-26|work=Land of 10|access-date=2018-04-11|language=en-US}}</ref> Edwards withdrew his name from the draft and returned for his junior season. On April 20, freshman Nojel Eastern announced he would also test the waters of the NBA draft without signing with an agent.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.btpowerhouse.com/2018/4/20/17257960/nojel-eastern-purdue-boilermakers-basketball-declares-2018-nba-draft-without-an-agent-scout-eval|title=Nojel Eastern Declares For 2018 NBA Draft Without An Agent|work=BT Powerhouse|access-date=2018-04-24}}</ref> Eastern also withdrew his name from the draft and returned to school.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/college/purdue/basketball/2018/05/30/nojel-easterns-nba-process-important-purdue-basketball-next-season/644934002/|title=Why Nojel Eastern's return from NBA draft consideration is important for Purdue basketball|work=Journal & Courier|access-date=2018-05-30|language=en}}</ref>

==Schedule and results==
The 2018–19 season will mark the first time in Big Ten history that the teams will play a 20-game conference schedule, setting a precedent for all Division I basketball.<ref name=":02">{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/big-ten-adds-two-games-for-a-20-game-conference-schedule-starting-in-2018-19/|title=Big Ten adds two games for a 20-game conference schedule starting in 2018–19 |last=Norlander|first=Matt|date=October 19, 2017|work=CBS Sports|access-date=March 9, 2018}}</ref> The new schedule will also include a regional component to increase the frequency of games among teams in similar areas. Over the course of a six-year cycle (12 playing opportunities), in-state rivals will play each other 12 times, regional opponents will play 10 times, and all other teams will play nine times.<ref name=":02" /> Three in-state series will be guaranteed home-and-homes: Illinois and Northwestern, Indiana and Purdue, and Michigan and Michigan State will always play twice.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21076233/big-ten-play-20-game-conference-schedule-next-season|title=Big Ten to move to 20-game conference slate |work=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-03-12}}</ref> Purdue announced a home and home series with [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] on May 17, 2018, to be played in [[Frank Erwin Center|Austin]] in 2018 and in West Lafayette in 2019.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.purduesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/051718aaa.html|title=Game at Texas Highlights Non-Con Slate|access-date=2018-05-18}}</ref>
